transcript: Meeting header: 2026-11-08 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~46 min | Attendees: Jordan, Priya (Redwood) — Maya, Ethan, Samir (HelixCare)
[00:00:00] Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is more of a casual interview / recording for marketing — HelixCare's launch story — if any of you need to stop recording just say so.
[00:00:12] Maya Lopez: Yep, all good on our end. We're excited — it's been a whirlwind month.
[00:00:18] Samir Patel: Quick note — we might clip a few sections for socials so heads up — nothing super sensitive.
[00:00:25] Jordan Kim: Perfect. Priya, do you want to kick off with a couple of quick technical questions so we can sprinkle that into the narrative?
[00:00:33] Priya Desai: Sure. Maya, Ethan — could you briefly describe the integration path? Was it Redwood API hosted, dedicated, VPC? Any gotchas?

[00:00:45] Ethan Zhao: We went hosted at first, then moved one critical route to Dedicated for predictability. I can spell out the sequence — we used the REST SDK, and the Redwood team helped pin model versions for our canary. There were a couple of tokenization quirks with our templated prompts — minor but worth mentioning.

[00:01:05] Maya Lopez: On the PM side, the reason we phased Dedicated was because marketing needed that sub-200ms tail for live personalization — users notice. We started with hosted to iterate, then when volume spiked we locked a reserved pool.
[00:01:20] Jordan Kim: That's a great soundbite — "started hosted, locked Dedicated when live personalization hit scale" — we'll flag that for the case video.
[00:01:30] Samir Patel: Also, we leaned on Redwood's batching suggestions. Priya sent a recommended batch window that cut cost — not dramatic but it preserved latency while saving tokens.
[00:01:45] Priya Desai: Yup — we recommended a 60ms continuous batch for their 2-3 concurrent session profile; that reduced per-token CPU overhead and kept 95th pct latency within SLO.
[00:02:00] Maya Lopez: Can I interject — when we say 'saved tokens' I mean saved cost. Marketing noticed this in the P&L because our cost per request dropped about 12% month-over-month after tuning.
[00:02:14] Jordan Kim: Nice, concrete number — "12% cost drop after tuning" — that'll help the case study credibility.

[00:02:20] Ethan Zhao: There's also the KV-cache win. We used Redwood's prefix caching for repeated patient-intake prompts; that reduced repeated context re-encoding and shaved off latencies on repeat flows.

[00:02:36] Samir Patel: Little anecdote — during the pilot demo the CEO asked 'is it fast enough?' and Maya just showed the flow live and it was under a second — he nodded and that sealed exec buy-in.
[00:02:50] Jordan Kim: Love that — exec moment. We should ask Maya to record a short one-liner about that for the video.
[00:03:00] Maya Lopez: I can do that. I'll give you a couple of options — one for exec-facing, one for the case study.
[00:03:10] Priya Desai: Shifting to security — HelixCare handles PHI. Ethan, quick summary on how you evaluated Redwood's Private / Hosted tradeoffs?

[00:03:22] Ethan Zhao: We did an internal risk review. Initially we ruled out hosted for patient workflows but Redwood allowed us to maintain a private VPC for the ingestion pipeline while using hosted for anonymized marketing prompts. Then for sensitive flows we planned private deployment, but the short-term path was hybrid — that flexibility was key.
[00:03:40] Jordan Kim: Great nuance — hybrid approach. That will help other regulated customers relate.

[00:03:48] Samir Patel: Switching gears — marketing results. We ran a 3-week A/B where the experimental group saw personalized onboarding messages powered by Redwood. Results: activation up 9%, retention at 7 days up 4 percentage points. I'll send the deck slide after this call.
[00:04:04] Jordan Kim: Can you repeat the exact percent numbers for the transcript so we capture them correctly?
[00:04:09] Samir Patel: Sure — Activation lift: +9% (p<0.05), Day-7 retention lift: +4.0 percentage points, and click-through on welcome emails improved by 18%.
[00:04:22] Priya Desai: Those are compelling. Did you run into any model quality regressions or hallucination problems?

[00:04:28] Maya Lopez: For the onboarding flow we kept the model outputs heavily templated and used structured function calls for certain fields — so hallucination was minimal. There were edge cases where jurisdictional language needed human review, but that's expected.
[00:04:44] Jordan Kim: Nice mention of function calls — we'll include that technical detail in the writeup.

[00:04:50] Ethan Zhao: On infra — our engineering lead noted memory pressure when sequence lengths spiked; Redwood's SE advised a slightly lower max tokens and better prefix pruning; that fixed the OOMs.
[00:04:59] Priya Desai: I sent that pruning patch and the team applied it within 48 hours — turnaround was quick.
[00:05:08] Maya Lopez: For the marketing video, we want the tone friendly and concrete. Short snippets, no heavy technical jargon — though we want to call out security and the measurable lift.
[00:05:20] Jordan Kim: Understood. We'll craft a 90-second hero video with two customer lines, one metric overlay, and a call-to-action to the case study landing page.
[00:05:30] Samir Patel: We'll also want the embed-ready quote for the site. Something like 'Redwood let us ship personalization fast, and it moved the needle — +9% activation.'
[00:05:39] Maya Lopez: I can approve that wording, maybe tweak to "shipped personalization in 3 weeks" — timeline resonates with our execs.
[00:05:48] Jordan Kim: Timeline + metric — good combo.
[00:05:55] [00:12:00] NOTE: small gap in transcript where recording skipped for ~30s during background bandwidth blip — speakers continued briefly (crosstalk).
[00:12:30] Jordan Kim: Quick rapid-fire: any surprised learnings?
[00:12:35] Maya Lopez: Honestly, growth saw that more personalized messages required fewer follow-up nudges — it was surprisingly sticky.
[00:12:44] Samir Patel: Ops appreciated the rollout controls — canarying per-region avoided a big blast radius during launch.
[00:12:52] Ethan Zhao: One caution — we did see slightly higher egress on Dedicated due to synchronous tooling; we offset with a caching layer and some server-side aggregation.
[00:13:05] Priya Desai: For the public-facing case study, we should avoid deep infra numbers but call out that we met latency SLOs and reduced cost via batching and caching.
[00:13:16] Jordan Kim: Agreed. Last formal question: do you have a one- or two-sentence lesson for other startups attempting a similar launch?
[00:13:26] Maya Lopez: Start with hosted to iterate, instrument everything, then move critical paths to Dedicated — and prioritize brief QA for sensitive language. That's our two-liner.
[00:13:36] Samir Patel: And measure activation early — even small percentage lifts compound.
[00:13:42] Jordan Kim: Awesome. We'll capture both of those as pull quotes.
[00:13:50] [00:20:00] — casual banter about day-to-day, team shout-outs, editing notes — omitted for brevity —

[00:28:10] Jordan Kim: Recap & next steps: Jordan will edit a 2-minute cut and share for approval; Priya will send the integration notes + perf spreadsheet; Maya will send a quote and logo. Anything to add?
[00:28:30] Maya Lopez: Please include that we anonymized PHI in the screenshot — legal asked that to be explicit.
[00:28:38] Ethan Zhao: I'll coordinate with our legal team to clear the quote if needed.
[00:28:45] Samir Patel: I'll follow up with the slide deck (A/B results) in the CRM.
[00:28:52] Jordan Kim: Great — we'll aim to publish a draft landing page by 2026-11-20. Jordan notes: permissions + final quote by 11/15.
[00:29:05] Priya Desai: Also sending the latency spreadsheet now — expect an email with the CSV and a quick readme.
[00:29:15] [00:45:30] Closing: quick pleasantries, thanks all — recording stopped.
